passages.text: One day Ruth’s mother-in-law Naomi said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you?
passages.sermon:
Naomi was Ruth’s mother-in-law.
Naomi spoke to Ruth.
Naomi said, “My daughter, I want good things for you.
I should look for a place where you can find rest.
I want you to have a secure and happy future.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ נָעֳמִ֣י חֲמוֹתָ֑הּ בִּתִּ֞י הֲלֹ֧א אֲבַקֶּשׁ־ לָ֛ךְ מָנ֖וֹחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽיטַב־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Now is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been working, a relative of ours? In fact, tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.
passages.sermon:
Boaz is a relative of ours.
You have been working with his servant girls.
Tonight, Boaz is winnowing barley.
He is doing this on the threshing floor.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה הֲלֹ֥א בֹ֙עַז֙ מֹֽדַעְתָּ֔נוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖ית אֶת־ נַעֲרוֹתָ֑יו הִנֵּה־ ה֗וּא זֹרֶ֛ה אֶת־ גֹּ֥רֶן הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים הַלָּֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: Therefore wash yourself, put on perfume, and wear your best clothes. Go down to the threshing floor, but do not let the man know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
passages.sermon:
Naomi spoke to Ruth, her daughter-in-law.
Naomi gave Ruth instructions.
Naomi said, “Wash yourself.”
Naomi said, “Put on perfume.”
Naomi said, “Wear your best clothes.”
Naomi said, “Go down to the threshing floor.”
Naomi said, “Do not let Boaz know you are there.”
Naomi said, “Wait until he has finished eating and drinking.”
passages.original: וְרָחַ֣צְתְּ׀ וָסַ֗כְתְּ וְשַׂ֧מְתְּ שִׂמְלֹתֵךְ עָלַ֖יִךְ וְיָרַדְתִּי הַגֹּ֑רֶן אַל־ תִּוָּדְעִ֣י לָאִ֔ישׁ עַ֥ד כַּלֹּת֖וֹ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go in and uncover his feet, and lie down, and he will explain to you what you should do.”
passages.sermon:
Boaz is a relative of ours.
Boaz will lie down to sleep on the threshing floor tonight.
Watch carefully and see where Boaz lies down.
Go to that place after he lies down.
Uncover Boaz’s feet.
Lie down there.
Boaz will tell you what you should do next.
passages.original: וִיהִ֣י בְשָׁכְב֗וֹ וְיָדַ֙עַתְּ֙ אֶת־ הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁכַּב־ שָׁ֔ם וּבָ֛את וְגִלִּ֥ית מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו וְשָׁכָבְתִּי וְהוּא֙ יַגִּ֣יד לָ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעַשִֽׂין׃

passages.text: “I will do everything you say,” Ruth answered.
passages.sermon: Ruth was a Moabite woman.\r\nRuth spoke to her mother-in-law Naomi.\r\nRuth said, “I will do everything you say.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלֶ֑יהָ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאמְרִ֥יֵַ֖ אֶֽעֱשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.
passages.sermon:
Ruth was a Moabite woman.
Naomi was her mother-in-law.
Naomi gave Ruth instructions.
Ruth went down to the threshing floor.
Ruth did everything Naomi told her to do.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֖רֶד הַגֹּ֑רֶן וַתַּ֕עַשׂ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ צִוַּ֖תָּה חֲמוֹתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: After Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then Ruth went in secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
passages.sermon:
Boaz was a man in Bethlehem.
Boaz finished eating.
Boaz finished drinking.
Boaz felt happy.
Boaz went to lie down.
Boaz lay at the end of the heap of grain.
Ruth was Naomi’s daughter-in-law.
Ruth went in quietly.
Ruth uncovered Boaz’s feet.
Ruth lay down.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אכַל בֹּ֤עַז וַיֵּשְׁתְּ֙ וַיִּיטַ֣ב לִבּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֕א לִשְׁכַּ֖ב בִּקְצֵ֣ה הָעֲרֵמָ֑ה וַתָּבֹ֣א בַלָּ֔ט וַתְּגַ֥ל מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו וַתִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

passages.text: At midnight, Boaz was startled, turned over, and there lying at his feet was a woman!
passages.sermon:
Boaz was a man of noble character.
It was midnight.
Boaz became startled.
He turned over.
He saw a woman lying at his feet.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד הָאִ֖ישׁ וַיִּלָּפֵ֑ת וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִשָּׁ֔ה שֹׁכֶ֖בֶת מַרְגְּלֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: “Who are you?” he asked. “I am your servant Ruth,” she replied. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.”
passages.sermon:
Boaz was a respected man in Bethlehem.
He saw a woman at his feet in the middle of the night.
Boaz asked, "Who are you?"
Ruth answered him.
She said, "I am Ruth."
She said, "I am your servant."
She asked Boaz to spread the corner of his garment over her.
She said, "You are a kinsman-redeemer."
A kinsman-redeemer is a close relative who can help or protect family members.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־ אָ֑תּ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ ר֣וּת אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ֤ כְנָפֶ֙ךָ֙ עַל־ אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ כִּ֥י גֹאֵ֖ל אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Then Boaz said, “May the LORD bless you, my daughter. You have shown more kindness now than before, because you have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.
passages.sermon:
Boaz was a respected man in Bethlehem.
Boaz spoke to Ruth.
Boaz said, “May the LORD bless you, my daughter.”
Boaz saw Ruth’s kindness.
Boaz said Ruth showed more kindness now than before.
Boaz said Ruth did not go after younger men.
Boaz said Ruth did not choose young men, whether they were poor or rich.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרוּכָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ לַֽיהוָה֙ בִּתִּ֔י הֵיטַ֛בְתְּ חַסְדֵּ֥ךְ הָאַחֲר֖וֹן מִן־ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן לְבִלְתִּי־ לֶ֗כֶת אַחֲרֵי֙ הַבַּ֣חוּרִ֔ים אִם־ דַּ֖ל וְאִם־ עָשִֽׁיר׃

passages.text: And now do not be afraid, my daughter. I will do for you whatever you request, since all my fellow townspeople know that you are a woman of noble character.
passages.sermon:
Boaz spoke to Ruth.
Boaz called Ruth “my daughter.”
Boaz told Ruth not to be afraid.
Boaz promised Ruth, “I will do for you whatever you ask.”
All the people at the town gate know Ruth.
They know Ruth is a woman of noble character.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה בִּתִּי֙ אַל־ תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאמְרִ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לָּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י יוֹדֵ֙עַ֙ כָּל־ שַׁ֣עַר עַמִּ֔י כִּ֛י אֵ֥שֶׁת חַ֖יִל אָֽתְּ׃

passages.text: Yes, it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.
passages.sermon:
Boaz spoke to Ruth.
Boaz was a kinsman-redeemer.
A kinsman-redeemer is a close relative who can help or rescue family members in need.
Boaz said, "It is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer."
Boaz also said, "There is another redeemer who is closer than I am."
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ כִּ֣י אָמְנָ֔ם כִּ֥י אם גֹאֵ֖ל אָנֹ֑כִי וְגַ֛ם יֵ֥שׁ גֹּאֵ֖ל קָר֥וֹב מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: Stay here tonight, and in the morning, if he wants to redeem you, good. Let him redeem you. But if he does not want to redeem you, as surely as the LORD lives, I will. Now lie here until morning.”
passages.sermon:
Boaz spoke to Ruth.
Boaz was a kinsman-redeemer.
Boaz said, “Stay here tonight.
In the morning, another man may want to redeem you.
If he wants to redeem you, let him do it.
If he does not want to redeem you, I will redeem you.
I promise this by the life of the LORD.
Now lie here until morning.”
passages.original: לִ֣ינִי׀ הַלַּ֗יְלָה וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ אִם־ יִגְאָלֵ֥ךְ טוֹב֙ יִגְאָ֔ל וְאִם־ לֹ֨א יַחְפֹּ֧ץ לְגָֽאֳלֵ֛ךְ וּגְאַלְתִּ֥יךְ אָנֹ֖כִי חַי־ יְהוָ֑ה שִׁכְבִ֖י עַד־ הַבֹּֽקֶר׃

passages.text: So she lay down at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone else could recognize her. Then Boaz said, “Do not let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.”
passages.sermon:
Ruth lay at Boaz’s feet until morning.
She got up before anyone could recognize another person.
Boaz spoke to her.
Boaz said, “Do not let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.”
passages.original: וַתִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מַרְגְּלֹתָו עַד־ הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַתָּ֕קָם בִּטְרוֹם יַכִּ֥יר אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַל־ יִוָּדַ֔ע כִּי־ בָ֥אָה הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַגֹּֽרֶן׃

passages.text: And he told her, “Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” When she did so, he shoveled six measures of barley into her shawl. Then he went into the city.
passages.sermon:
Boaz was a kind and generous man.
Boaz spoke to Ruth.
He said, “Bring the shawl you are wearing.
Hold it out.”
Ruth held out her shawl.
Boaz measured six measures of barley.
He placed the barley into her shawl.
Boaz then went into the city.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָ֠בִי הַמִּטְפַּ֧חַת אֲשֶׁר־ עָלַ֛יִךְ וְאֶֽחֳזִי־ בָ֖הּ וַתֹּ֣אחֶז בָּ֑הּ וַיָּ֤מָד שֵׁשׁ־ שְׂעֹרִים֙ וַיָּ֣שֶׁת עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיָּבֹ֖א הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: When Ruth returned to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked her, “How did it go, my daughter?” Then Ruth told her all that Boaz had done for her.
passages.sermon:
Ruth returned to her mother-in-law Naomi.
Naomi spoke to Ruth.
Naomi said, “How did it go, my daughter?”
Ruth told Naomi everything.
Ruth explained all that Boaz had done for her.
passages.original: וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל־ חֲמוֹתָ֔הּ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־ אַ֣תְּ בִּתִּ֑י וַתַּ֨גֶּד־ לָ֔הּ אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָֽשָׂה־ לָ֖הּ הָאִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: And she said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’ ”
passages.sermon: Ruth spoke to Naomi.\r\nRuth said, “He gave me these six measures of barley.”\r\nRuth explained, “He told me, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר שֵׁשׁ־ הַשְּׂעֹרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה נָ֣תַן לִ֑י כִּ֚י אָמַ֣רֵַ֔ אַל־ תָּב֥וֹאִי רֵיקָ֖ם אֶל־ חֲמוֹתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: “Wait, my daughter,” said Naomi, “until you find out how things go, for he will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today.”
passages.sermon:
Naomi spoke to Ruth.
Naomi is Ruth’s mother-in-law.
Naomi said, “Wait, my daughter.”
Naomi told Ruth to wait until she knows what will happen.
Naomi said Boaz will not rest today.
Naomi said Boaz will finish the matter today.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ שְׁבִ֣י בִתִּ֔י עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּֽדְעִ֔ין אֵ֖יךְ יִפֹּ֣ל דָּבָ֑ר כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשְׁקֹט֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ כִּֽי־ אִם־ כִּלָּ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַיּֽוֹם׃
